correctness.rationale: For the explicitly given seven-vertex graph with 11 edges, I independently recomputed CN(A), CN²-closed nonempty sets and their chains: 18 closed sets, 38 edges, 16 triangles. The induced involution A->CN(A) has no fixed simplices because A and CN(A) are disjoint. Independently enumerate free triangle-edge pairs in involution orbits and remove eight such orbits; all 16 triangles disappear, leaving an invariant free connected graph Q with 18 vertices/22 edges. Quotient edge/vertex orbits number 11/9; graph ranks are 5 and 3 before/after quotient. A connected free 1-dimensional graph admits an equivariant map to S1 by equivariant cellular extension, but not to S0 because connected, so Z2-index exactly one. The cited Csorba–Lange–Schurr–Wassmer equivariant box/Lovasz comparison transfers the index. Separate diamond argument forces chi>=4 and an explicit four-coloring shows chi=4. The theorem only concerns this exact finite graph and the equivariant collapse, NOT a new nonequivariant five-circle wedge statement.
